motion.name: road-canvas
motion.value: CRUISE 110 px/s steady; SEG 900 px per state (8 states, NJ to FL); TREE_GAP 22; end pause 2.5s at 30px past each house, then reverse; camera and lane ease dt*2, heading ease dt*3; road width 60 (canvas <700px) / 78; dpr cap 2; no input of any kind
motion.purpose: The one moving thing on the page: a packed car driving NJ to FL and back in the close. The hero roadside scene is a still drawing.

motion.name: seam-static
motion.value: wave y = 34 + 9 sin(x/190 + phi) + 5 sin(x/83 + 2 phi), phi = 1.7*index, sampled every 20 units; dash 26/22, stroke 3; drawn once
motion.purpose: Still lane line along each change of ground. Never animated.

motion.name: loop-and-reduced-motion
motion.value: one shared requestAnimationFrame loop, dt capped at 50ms, gated by IntersectionObserver; prefers-reduced-motion: single still canvas frame, scroll-behavior auto
motion.purpose: The car runs only on screen and never for users who opt out.

roadBand.placement: top of the close, full bleed, flush under the second seam (seam fill #173c33)

decisions.decision: Keep the night-drive vibe, adopt the 40-70 UX research brief's structure.
Allow one small labeled phones-only Call pill (999px, amber, 'Call Ed') as a per-site exception; full-width sticky bars and banners stay banned.

More colour: header and hero become one green guide sign (theme-color #0a6337, white clover); Meet your driver becomes a blue I-95 services sign (#17508f / #0f3c6c). Link hovers on the signs go amber; shield blue stays a response only.
Three photo slots for Ed (desktop hero wide 4:3, phone owner-line face 56px, driver-sign portrait 4:5), dashed placeholders until photos arrive.
Rate is $1 per mile: How it works step 1, the cost answer, the close lede. Not in the hero.

Hero becomes a still roadside scene at dusk: the green guide sign (with an outer green rim and drop shadow) stands on two posts above a road. Header returns to night with the leaf-green clover; theme-color back to #0e2a33.
Close: the amber Call button is removed; the big phone number is the call, with Send a text on touch devices only.

Dropped the blue services sign for Meet your driver: "the blue goes with nothing and the repeated signs feel ugly". Meet your driver is plain on aluminum, Ed's number in sign green; the hero is the only sign.

The yellow hero Call button was "obnoxiously bright": replaced by just the clickable phone number lettered on the sign (amber hover underline). The header phone number is removed. No Call button remains; amber at rest is only the phone Call pill and the road centre lines.

"Add some color to the text on the sign": new sign yellow --sun #ffd166 (4.9:1 on sign green), lettering only on the hero sign: headline line 2, hero phone icon, owner's name. The hero promise line is removed.
The hero sign hangs on an overhead gantry like a real interstate sign (from a photo Ellie sent) instead of standing on two posts. The phone number in Meet your driver is removed.

"Looks like a child's project... put more effort into the hero": hero scene detail pass. Sign face as one sheet with an inset border and sheen; stars, radial dusk glow, far hills and a pine/round-crown treeline; graded grass and road, sheen, haze, near darkening, gravel shoulders; two still far cars; darker backlit gantry steel with a Warren web, twin-chord legs and concrete footings. Panel seams tried and removed.
The two far cars get bodies: small inline SVG cars (oncoming front view with headlights, departing rear view with tail lights) sized to their lane at depth, replacing the radial-gradient light dots.

heroScene.ground: svg 1000x150 stretched, 150px (200px): grass gradient #2b4640 > #1b3a2d (18%) > #0c2418; shoulder #33403a (488-512 at the horizon to -290/1290); road gradient #6e6670 > #424a50 (14%) > #2a3236 (60%) > #1b2225; sheen radial #ffb070 .38 > 0 at the vanishing point; edge lines #e8ece6; amber #f6b638 centre dashes; haze #c9a294 .32 > 0 over the top 26 units; near darkening #000 0 at 55% > .28
heroScene.traffic: Two far cars as small inline SVGs (viewBox 40x24, 32-wide body) in .traffic (ground row, z-index 2), placed by left/top/width % and translate(-50%,-91.7%) so wheels sit on the road at depth and width is ~3/4 of the lane: oncoming (.car.on, front view, 48.15%/4%/3.25%) body #262f37, windshield #3e4a57>#7a6a6c, grille #151b20, headlamps #fff6dc with radial halo #fff3d2 .75 > #ffe9b8 .3 > 0 and a light pool on the road; away (.car.away, rear view, 52.85%/7%/5%) body #1c242a, rear window #2c3946>#4a4f5a, bumper line #11171b, plate #7d837f, tail lamps #ff3b30 with halo #ff4a3d .6 > .2 > 0; tyres #0b0f12; #000 contact shadow .35/.4. Physical lights, not UI glow; still.
heroScene.gantry: .scene grid (rows: sign, horizon band, ground; vars --leg 12px/20px, --edge 6.7%/9.3%, --foot 54px/80px). Truss 36px (52px) tall at the sign's vertical centre: top chord linear-gradient(#b4bec1,#5b676d), bottom chord linear-gradient(#8e999d,#4a555b), 3px (4px), with a Warren web plus verticals in #566369. Legs var(--leg) wide: twin chords 3px (4px) linear-gradient(90deg,#4f5b61,#b4bec1 55%,#5b676d) and (90deg,#4f5b61,#9aa5a9 45%,#4a555b) with a diagonal-and-rung web; .leg.up rises calc(50% + 24px) (+34px); .leg.dn spans the band and ground above it (z-index 3), feet --foot above the bottom; concrete footing linear-gradient(#9aa29c,#6c746f) 7px tall, 4px wider each side, plus footing-shadow.

narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Night Drive Down I-95"**

The whole page is one drive down I-95. It opens at the roadside at dusk: a green interstate guide sign hangs from an overhead steel gantry spanning the road, under a starlit sky fading from night blue to a warm glow on the horizon, and interstate green is also shamrock green, so the mark and the road share one colour. The sign appears once. Ed introduces himself plainly on aluminum. The light "sign-back aluminum" run reads like the back of a road sign: cool, matte, plain. The close is the highway after dark: blue-green, never black, with the car driving it. Headlight amber is the only warm light on the page. At rest it belongs to calling and to the road's centre line, and nothing else in the interface; the dusk glow on the hero's horizon is scenery.

The page is calm and plainly structured. Its readers are mostly 40 to 70, on a phone, often inside Facebook's in-app browser. After a UX research brief for that audience, Ellie kept the I-95 world and adopted a plainer structure. On 2026-10-15 she asked for more colour, which put the hero on a green guide sign that now stands in a still roadside scene at dusk. A blue services sign for the driver, tried the same day, was dropped: "the blue goes with nothing and the repeated signs feel ugly". Later that day she replaced the amber hero Call button, "obnoxiously bright", with the clickable number itself, and removed the number from the header. The hero sign holds a large headline (its second line, "I'll drive.", in sign yellow), the phone number lettered on the sign as the call itself, a plain "or send a text" link, and the owner's name, in sign yellow, beside a slot for his photo. Then come a plain meet-the-driver block, three numbered steps, plain questions including cost, and a close that opens on the road band with the car driving it, then a big phone number. On phones a small Call pill is never far away. The car is the one moving thing on the page. The road is scenery to watch, not a toy: it takes no touch, the page scrolls straight over it, and nothing on the page asks to be tapped open. Body text is 18px, every call and text control is at least 48px tall (the Send a text button 58px), every word is visible on arrival, and nothing depends on hover.

The world rejects the trucking-company template: no fleet photos, no quote forms, no badges. Type is the system font stack set heavy (700–850), which is Ellie's pitch-site house style. Section headlines are uppercase; the hero headline is mixed case.
keyCharacteristics: One interstate sign carries the colour: the hero is a green guide sign hung on an overhead gantry over a road at dusk. The header sits on night above the scene; then come one long cool-aluminum run (Meet your driver included) and a blue-green night close. No pure black anywhere as a surface.
One sign, once: the green guide sign with its 3px sign-white face border is the hero, and nothing else on the page is a sign panel.
One warm colour, amber, reserved at rest for the phone Call pill and the road centre lines. There is no Call button: wherever the page asks for a call, the number itself is the link.
Shield blue appears only when something is hovered or focused.
Three photo slots wait for Ed: a wide photo in the desktop hero, a round face beside the owner line on phones, a portrait beside Ed's introduction.
Only the car in the close moves. The hero's roadside scene, seams, sections and text are still.
Everything is visible: no accordions, no tabs, no tap-to-reveal.
The phone number is always written out, and on phones a small Call pill is never far away.
Heavy system sans with big tap targets, built for older eyes and thumbs.

rules.name: The One Headlight Rule
rules.body: At rest, amber is used only for the phone Call pill and the road centre lines (the canvas centre dash, the centre dashes of the hero road, and the lane line on the seams). Its one other interface job is a response: the hero number and the hero text link take an amber hover underline, because they sit on the green sign, where shield blue would sink. Every other link hovers in shield blue (deep shield blue on aluminum). Don't use amber at rest for buttons, links, borders, icons or headings. Outside the interface amber appears only as scenery: the warm end of the dusk glow behind the hero's treeline, and the cargo in the two car drawings, which is what "packed" looks like at that size.

rules.name: The Shield Blue Only Responds Rule
rules.body: Interstate-shield blue appears only as a response to the pointer or keyboard: hover borders and underlines, focus outlines (shield blue on night, deep shield blue on aluminum). It is never at rest: never a ground, a fill, or a link colour.

rules.name: The Never Black Rule
rules.body: Dark grounds are blue-green night (night, night-2), or guide green, never #000. Black appears only as low-alpha shading: inside the canvas, and in the hero scene as the sign's tight drop shadow, its sheen's shaded corner, the footing shadows, and the near darkening of the ground. The Call pill's shadow is night-tinted.

rules.name: The System Stack Rule
rules.body: Ellie's house style: the native system sans and nothing else on this site. Hierarchy comes from weight, size, and case.

rules.name: The Number Is Written Out Rule
rules.body: Wherever the page asks someone to call, the number 732-300-3835 is visible in text and is itself the tap-to-call link: on the hero sign, in the close, and in the footer. It is not in the header, not in Meet your driver, and not inside a button. The Call pill is the one place it lives only in the accessible label, because the pill must stay small.

rules.name: The Two Buttons Max Rule
rules.body: A contact group holds at most two controls: the phone number as a link first, then, on touch devices only, a way to text. The hero pairs the number lettered on the sign with a plain "or send a text" link; the close pairs the big number with a Send a text outline button. Text controls are hidden on mouse devices, where `sms:` does nothing. Don't add a third channel, a duplicate, or a Call button to a group.

rules.name: The No Sticky Bar, One Small Pill Rule
rules.body: No full-width sticky or fixed bars or banners, ever. A single small labeled Call pill is allowed on phones only: amber, fully rounded, "Call Ed", pinned 16px from the bottom-right corner (plus the safe-area inset). It shows only after the hero call group has scrolled away and hides while the close number is on screen, so it never doubles a visible call. This is a deliberate per-site exception Ellie made on 2026-10-14 for this 40–70 audience; it does not carry to other sites.

rules.name: The Nothing Hidden Behind A Tap Rule
rules.body: No accordions, tabs, carousels, "read more" or tap-to-reveal. Every question shows its answer in full and every step shows its text. If text is worth having on the page, it is visible on arrival; if it isn't, cut it.

rules.name: The Sign And The Pill Stand Up Rule
rules.body: Only the hero sign and the floating Call pill get elevation. Buttons, links, step discs, lists, question pairs, photo slots and sections stay flat.

rules.name: The One Moving Thing Rule
rules.body: Only the car in the close moves. The hero roadside scene (sky and stars, glow, sign, gantry, hills and treeline, road, the two far cars), seams, text, illustrations and sections never animate, reveal on scroll, or loop. The only other changes on the page are state feedback (colour shifts and a 1px press) in direct response to a touch, hover or keyboard focus, and the Call pill's short fade in and out, which is switched off under reduced motion.

dos: **Do** sign the page like I-95, once: the hero as a green guide sign hung on an overhead gantry over the road, as one sheet of green with its sign-white border set 10px inside the edge.

**Do** keep amber at rest for the Call pill and the centre lines; the hero number and text link, on the green sign, take an amber hover underline, and every other link hovers in shield blue. Text on amber is always ink.
**Do** keep sign yellow as lettering on the hero sign only: the headline's second line, the phone icon, the owner's name.
**Do** write the phone number out wherever the page asks for a call, and make the number itself the link.
**Do** show shield blue only on hover (gated behind `(hover:hover)`) and focus. Use deep shield blue on aluminum and sign-white focus in the header and the hero.
**Do** keep each photo slot's shape when Ed's photo lands: 4:3 at 12px for the wide hero photo, a 56px circle for the face, 4:5 at 8px for the portrait, image set to cover.
**Do** stitch every change of ground with a still seam whose fill is the next ground's colour.
**Do** keep reading text at 18px or larger, tap targets at 48px or more, the Send a text button at 58px and the Call pill at 56px.
**Do** show every answer and every step in full, on arrival.
**Do** keep the car the only moving thing: run it on the shared loop, pause it off screen, and draw a still frame under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
**Do** write icons as inline SVG symbols that inherit `currentColor`.
donts: **Don't** add a second moving thing: no rolling seams, scroll reveals, marquees, looping illustrations, or extra traffic in the road.
**Don't** make the road band interactive or capture touch on it. It is scenery; the page must scroll over it.
**Don't** hide text behind a tap: no accordions, tabs, carousels or "read more".
**Don't** add a full-width sticky or fixed bar or banner, ever. The one allowed floating element is the small labeled Call pill on phones.
**Don't** put more than two contact controls in a group, bring back an amber Call button, or use amber at rest for anything but the Call pill and the centre lines.
**Don't** use shield blue at rest as a link colour, accent, fill or ground.
**Don't** add a second sign panel (a blue driver sign was tried and dropped), or animate anything in the hero scene: the sign, gantry, horizon, road and far cars are a still drawing.
**Don't** hand the site over with a dashed placeholder still in a photo slot.
**Don't** use sign yellow off the hero sign, as a fill, border or underline, or in place of amber for calling.
**Don't** use #000 or near-black as a ground. Night is blue-green.
**Don't** put a tracked uppercase label above a headline. The page has no tracked uppercase text.

**Don't** add shadows to buttons, links, step discs, lists, question pairs or sections. Only the hero sign and the Call pill stand up, and don't spread hard offset blocks like the one behind the portrait to other elements.
**Don't** use stock fleet photos, quote forms, or trust badges.
